ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL (FIXED by testing agent). Importing { Circle } from 'phosphor-react-native' (v3.0.6) returns undefined because that package only exports `CircleIcon` for the Circle glyph (unlike every other icon used in the app which ships a deprecated old-name alias). This crashed RecordCard with 'Element type is invalid ... Check the render method of RecordCard' the moment select mode was enabled, blocking the entire Bulk Export flow. Fix applied: `import { ..., CheckCircle, CircleIcon as Circle } from 'phosphor-react-native'` (record-card.tsx:2). Please verify and consider grepping the codebase for other bare `Circle` imports.

The record-card-RCP-2026-000001 testID renders TWICE in the DOM (query_selector_all returns 2 nodes while only 1 is visible). This is a FlatList virtualization/measurement artifact on web but it caused Playwright taps on the card in select mode to hit a non-interactive clone, so selection didn't increment the count. User impact on real devices is nil (only the visible node responds to touch), but consider a `getItemLayout` or removing the duplicate render to make automated tests reliable.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py agents endpoints (L466-496) correctly scope by user_id, strip _id in projections, validate empty name -> 422, and return {ok: true} + 404 on delete-of-unknown; matches spec.
server.py PUT /tag-colors (L508-516) correctly drops keys/values that are empty/whitespace and upserts per user; GET returns {} initially — matches spec exactly.

server.py list_records date filter (L384-391) uses string comparison on ISO-8601 `created_at` and pads end with `T23:59:59.999999+00:00`. That works for our stored ISO strings but is fragile: if any record's created_at ever loses the trailing '+00:00' or uses a different offset, comparison could go wrong. Prefer storing created_at as a native BSON datetime and comparing datetime objects.

record-card.tsx imports both `Record` and `Record2` from src/api as pure types — babel-typescript strips them at build time so no runtime harm, but naming a local type `Record` shadows JS's global `Record<K,V>` inside this file; consider renaming to `RecordDoc` and `TagColorMap` for clarity.
records.tsx computes `start` from DATE_FILTERS.days but never sends an `end`, so 7d/30d/90d work as expected (>= start). Good.

rca_of_issue: RecordCard Element-type crash (fixed): `phosphor-react-native@3.0.6` renamed its default named icon exports to *Icon (e.g. `Circle` -> `CircleIcon`) and left deprecated aliases only for the icons that already had a stable public API. `Circle` was NOT given a deprecation alias — its .js only contains `export { I as CircleIcon }`, so `import { Circle } from 'phosphor-react-native'` resolves to `undefined`. That's fine at compile time but blows up React's `createElement(Circle, ...)` at render time with the observed 'expected a string or class/function but got undefined'. Reproduction: navigate to Records tab, tap `records-select` — RecordCard's unselected-checkbox branch renders `<Circle .../>` and throws. Fix (applied): change the import to `CircleIcon as Circle`. Alternative acceptable fixes: use `CircleIcon` directly, or swap to another phosphor glyph like `CircleDashed` (has the deprecated alias).
